newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey Islamist urges Ciller graft vote repeat.
newsitem.headline: Turkey Islamist urges Ciller graft vote repeat.

text.p: A leading Turkish Islamist MP on Wednesday called for a repeat of a disputed parliamentary vote that cleared Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller of corruption charges.
"The result is not clear and it is a situation in which the vote has to be repeated," Welfare Party deputy Salih Kapusuz told a news conference.

A parliament committee is to meet later this week to review Tuesday's vote in which MPs narrowly decided against setting up an inquiry into allegations that Ciller was involved in graft at a state-run hotel and tourism company.

The opposition says two or three government MPs were counted as having voted for Ciller despite not being in attendance. It also says one vote against Ciller was found on the floor of the debating hall after the result was announced.
The vote could have caused a rift in the Islamist-led coalition government if Welfare MPs had swayed it against Ciller, who also the foreign minister.
Deputy speaker Yasin Hatipoglu originally announced that Ciller has won the ballot by 247 to 242 but parliament officials later revised the number of votes in favour of her to 244.
Ciller recently avoided being sent to the Supreme Court in three alleged corruption cases with the help of Welfare MPs who voted to drop the charges.
Most MPs of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare party again backed Ciller in the latest vote but a group of around 20 defied the premier's orders to back her.
